title: Fed-key models (plain/cipher autokey, idea-74 lag patterns, sculpture and K1-K3 running keys) tested on every Latin-square tableau, on one hidden alphabet, and with the key read on A-Z/KRYPTOS
k4_result: Part A (any tableau with distinct rows and columns, clue blocks in place): 91 of 200 fixed models are impossible on every tableau: plain autokey back 1-4, ahead 1-6, back/ahead 42; cipher autokey back 1-11, 13-31, 33, 35, 42, 49, 50, 53, 55, 58, 65 and ahead 1-29, 31, 35, 42, 49, 53-56, 62, 63, 67. 37 of the 91 need two or more wrong clue letters to escape; 54 would be saved by one. Every cipher-feed lag below 30 dies except 12 back. Idea-74 lag patterns that survive: plain feed 28/64 (p=2) to 972,236/2,097,152 (p=7); cipher feed 9/400 (p=2), 78/8,000, 1,355/160,000, 30,986/3.2M, 566,609/64M, about 13.7M/1.28e9 (p=7, sampled). Running keys: 45,810 of 2,762,382 sculpture-reading offsets (1.66%) and 61 of 3,292 K1-K3 text offsets survive. The low survival comes from positions 27 and 65 (plain R, cipher P both times): on any tableau the key letters there must be equal. Part B (one hidden alphabet on all sides, 4 forms): every running-key survivor is impossible (183,240 sculpture and 244 text systems); no cipher-autokey system has a solution with distinct places (468 impossible, 76 too loose to decide); plain-autokey chains at lags 19-22: 18 impossible, 0 with solutions, 14 undecided. Part C (key on A-Z or KRYPTOS): all running-key systems impossible; 2 (A-Z) and 4 (KR) cipher-autokey systems have solutions, and none of them decrypts 10 or more quadgrams outside the clues. No K4 reading to score. Clue 2 moved by -3..+3: 63-91 models impossible, the same picture.
controls: 50 shuffled K4s at the true clue placement. Models impossible on every tableau: 40-129, median 62. K4's 91 is higher than 39 of the 50 (plain autokey: K4 12, controls 10-23; cipher autokey: K4 79, controls 30-106). 15 of 50 controls also have one clue pair with the same plain and cipher letter. Sculpture running-key survivors: 26,295-1,242,169 (median 945,625; K4 45,810). Cipher-feed lag patterns p=2: 0-211 (median 136; K4 9). Part B: cipher-autokey systems with solutions 0-10 (median 1; K4 0); running-key systems with solutions: 0 in every control (K1-K3 texts all offsets; sculpture readings on a sample of 3,000 survivors for 5 controls). Chains impossible 17-42 (median 31; K4 35). Best control reading from listed solutions: -6.36 per quadgram over 10 quadgrams (noise).
planted: Latin square: 6/6 (plain autokey lag 3, cipher autokey lag 11, K2 plaintext running key, two random 26x26 Latin squares that are not group tables): the true model never clashes, while 82-133 of 199 other fixed models and 244-316 of 316 other K2 offsets clash. Hidden alphabet: 8/8 cipher-lag-11 and K2-running-key systems (Parts B and C) list the true alphabet. 4/4 plain-autokey-lag-3 systems keep the true alphabet (it satisfies the equations, never reported impossible), but 18 equations are too few to list it uniquely.
scope_limits: The count is mostly lag patterns: per ciphertext and clue placement there are 200 fixed models, 1.35e9 cipher-feed and 2.4e6 plain-feed lag patterns, and 2.77e6 running-key offsets; these are summed over K4, 50 controls and 7 placements. Part A covers only keys whose letters inside the clues are themselves known letters of K4 or of a given text. Keys from words, numbers or unknown texts are outside it. The tableau must have distinct rows and columns, and the key letter must pick the row by a fixed one-to-one rule (an added constant is allowed). A model that survives is undecided, not supported. Plain autokey at lags 13-29 has no known triple and is not decided (Part B chains cover lags 15-26 on one hidden alphabet only). Lag patterns: plain lags 1-8, cipher lags 1-20, period 2-7, Part A only; p=7 cipher was sampled (200,000 patterns). Running keys: attack 58's grids and walks with every d-th letter for d=1-60, plus the K1, K2 (also corrected), K3 and joined K1-K3 plaintexts forwards and reversed; the key must cover the whole clue span. Parts B/C: one alphabet on all three sides (B), or plain/cipher on one hidden alphabet with the key on A-Z/KRYPTOS (C), four +- forms, one constant; no multiplier. Undecided systems (too loose to list) are not excluded. Controls for Parts B/C were run only at the true clue placement, and the sculpture readings only on a sample. No transposition before or after.

negative.hypothesis: K4 is a plaintext or ciphertext autokey (fixed lag, or an idea-74 lag pattern) or a running key from the sculpture or K1-K3 texts, on some tableau with distinct rows and columns, possibly a hidden one.
negative.scope: Any Latin-square tableau (Part A): plain autokey lags 1-60 and cipher autokey lags 1-68, back and ahead; idea-74 lag patterns p 2-7 (plain lags 1-8, cipher lags 1-20); attack-58 sculpture readings (every d-th letter, d 1-60) and the K1-K3 plaintexts forwards and reversed at every offset; BERLINCLOCK also moved by -3..+3. One hidden alphabet on all sides (Part B, 4 forms) and the key on A-Z/KRYPTOS with a hidden plain/cipher alphabet (Part C) for the same fixed models and running-key survivors, plus plain-autokey chains at lags 15-26.
negative.outcome: Dead in scope: 91 of 200 fixed models are impossible on every tableau, including all plain autokey at lags 1-4 back and 1-6 ahead, and every cipher autokey below lag 30 except 12 back (37 of the 91 survive any single wrong clue letter). Every surviving sculpture or K1-K3 running key and every cipher autokey has no solution on one hidden alphabet. Plain autokey at lags 5-12 back, 7-12 ahead and 30-52 (other than 42), the lag patterns, and cipher lags 12 back and 30-68 survive only as undecided. Controls: 40-129 models impossible (median 62; K4 91, ordinary). Planted 6/6 on Latin squares; hidden alphabet listed 8/8, kept 4/4.

follow_ups: Positions 27 and 65 both have plain R and cipher P, so on ANY tableau the key letters at 27 and 65 must be equal. That is a one-line test for every key source: a running key, word key or period must give the same letter 38 places apart (periods 2, 19 and 38 always do). Run it as a cheap gate on every key list in data/ before the costlier tests.

The undecided plain-autokey lags (5-12 back, 7-12 ahead, 30-52) and cipher lags 12 back and 30-68 could be settled on one hidden alphabet if the equations were tied to idea-93 dictionary alphabets on one side only (half-hidden).
